structs.name: bfx__Task
structs.size_evidence: method 2 + method 7: bfx::Task::scalar_deleting_dtor@0x141fbb260 is slot 0 of ??_7Task@bfx@@6B@ (0x1426831a8), the vftable that bfx::Task::Task@0x141fbaf10 stores at +0; it calls bdMemory__deallocate_5 with edx=10h (sized delete 16). Derived SimulateTask: bfx_AsyncSim_CreateTask@0x141fac310 and bfx_System_SimulateAsync@0x141fac8c0 allocate 32 bytes, call bfx::Task::Task, then store system at +16 and deltaTime at +24, so the first own member of SimulateTask is at 16.
members: bfx::Task::Task@0x141fbaf10: lea rax, ??_7Task vftable; mov [rcx], rax (also stored by ~Task@0x141fbb0d0 and scalar_deleting_dtor@0x141fbb260)
bfx::Task::Task@0x141fbaf10: mov [rcx+8], rdx; ~Task@0x141fbb0d0: mov rcx,[rcx+8] then DisconnectFromTask; bfx_AsyncSim_CreateTask passes the 16-byte proxy as rdx

optional rename to __vftable (game-test name); same offset and type
structs.notes: The IDA layout's 24-byte size and m_pNext are not Replay facts; the first pass guessed 16 and that is now proven. The vftable symbol's later slots (_purecall, then slots that belong to other classes, e.g. RemoteFunctionCaller dtor at slot 3) show the symbol is shared with neighbours, so only slots 0 and 1 are Task's own. The sized-delete lead is validated: the sized delete with 16 is in Task's own vtable slot 0.

structs.name: bfx__Link
structs.size_evidence: Size proven at 128 (not used here because the verdict is partial): bfx::LinkBase::LinkBase@0x141fcca20 writes a self pointer to this+120 (mov [this+120]) and the qword at +112, so sizeof(LinkBase) >= 128; bfx::LinkStripImpl::Create@0x141fce340 calls LinkBase::LinkBase(v11) and then stores its own startAnchor at v11+128, so the derived first member starts at 128 (method 7). Link::Enable@0x141fc6ac0, SetLayerMask@0x141fca8d0 and SetLinkDat@0x141fca990 all end with a tail jump to the LinkBase method with the same this, so a Link object has the LinkBase layout.
members: LinkBase::LinkBase@0x141fcca20: *this = bfx::LinkBase vftable (base-class bytes 0..15 are HandleTargetBase / LinkBase; not mine)
LinkBase::LinkBase@0x141fcca20: *(this+16) = owner; Link::Enable@0x141fc6ac0: rax = [this+10h], then [rax+10h] -> [..+8] is passed to bfx__LogLinkEnable as recorderOwner

LinkBase::LinkBase@0x141fcca20: mov [this+104], linkId (4th argument). Link::Enable@0x141fc6ac0: mov edx,[rdi+68h] is the linkId log argument; SetLayerMask@0x141fca8d0 and SetLinkDat@0x141fca990 use the same field as linkId. The IDA name m_layerMask is wrong: SetLayerMask keeps its layerMask argument in edx and passes it to LinkBase::SetLayerMask, never storing it at +104
changed_members: rename to m_linkId, type unsigned int (CONFIRMED by LinkBase ctor and the three Link methods; game-test has no bfx::Link layout, so this is a proposal, not a rename)
retype unsigned __int64 -> void * (same size) and rename m_owner: it is the owner pointer, not a handle
delete from bfx__Link: the Link object ends at 128. In the derived LinkStripImpl the bytes at +128 are startAnchor (OWORD), not a Link member
unconfirmed: bfx::Link is the Replay object whose vtable is LinkBase's (its methods forward to LinkBase). The type name bfx::Link vs bfx::LinkBase is not resolved here; the objects come from a table walked in bfx_ReplayEvent_Planner@0x141ffd978 (mov rdi,[rbx]; call Link::Enable)

+24 (pointer, set to this+120 when zero), +32, +40 (dword from a global byte), +48..+95 (48 bytes copied from linkDesc), +100 (flags dword), +112 (qword zero), +120 (self pointer): all written by LinkBase::LinkBase, not Link methods. Their names belong to bfx::LinkBase, which is not in my entry; they are not placed here
structs.notes: Verdict partial because the bytes 24..127 are the LinkBase layout that LinkBase::LinkBase fills, and that struct is outside my entry; the size 128 is proven. The coordinator can resolve bfx__Link to 128 bytes together with LinkBase. The IDA 136-byte size and m_subObject128 are not Link facts.
